issues.display_title: Issue #1716: feat(panoramas): enforce Pro/Agency subscription on POST /panoramas/change-placeid
issues.main_description_html:
What

POST /panoramas/change-placeid (Edit Pano Place ID on the dashboard's Edit Panorama page) is being restricted to Pro and Agency subscribers.

The dashboard side is covered by GoThruMedia/gothru-dashboard#4165, but that gate is UI-only and trivially bypassable. The API has to enforce it too.

Current state

  • The route is registered outside the auth middleware group in routes/panoramaRoutes.php.
  • Because of that, ChangePanoPlaceIdController reads user_id straight from the request body instead of the token.
  • ChangePanoPlaceIdAction only checks moderation ownership. No subscription check at all.

⚠️ Please verify first: the dashboard never sends user_id in the body, so the ownership check may currently be receiving 0 and rejecting every legitimate request. If that's the case, this task also fixes a live bug — confirm the actual behaviour on staging/production before starting.

Requested changes

  1. Move the route into the auth middleware group so user_id and subscribtion come from the verified token, not from client input.
  2. In the action, after the ownership check, reject the request when the user is not on a Pro or Agency plan.
  3. Allowed plans: Pro (1), Pro Yearly (6), Agency (5), Agency Yearly (8), Sub-account (4).

    ❓ Confirm whether Sub-account should be allowed. The dashboard task assumes yes.

  4. Return a clear domain error for the rejection (new domain code + HTTP status), consistent with how the other panorama exceptions are handled. Don't reuse PANORAMA.NOT_OWNER — the reason is different.
  5. Add the error message to the translation files.

Notes

  • App\Helpers\Tours\SubscriptionHelper already exists but its list is "any active paid plan" (includes Basic). Pro/Agency is a different, narrower set — add a separate method rather than changing the existing one, since other actions depend on it.
  • Update the endpoint docs (docs/v2/panoramas/change-placeid.md) — auth requirement, new error row, and the fact that user_id is no longer a body field.

Done when

  • Request without a valid token → 401.
  • Pro / Agency / Sub-account user, owns the tour → Place ID updates as before.
  • Basic or pay-as-you-go user, owns the tour → rejected with the new subscription error, Place ID unchanged.
  • Sending someone else's user_id in the body has no effect — identity comes from the token only.
  • Dashboard's existing call still works unchanged for eligible users.
  • Docs updated.

Related

  • Frontend: GoThruMedia/gothru-dashboard#4165

Dev Note — After Implementation

Done in PR #1719.

  • The suspected live bug is confirmed. The route sat outside auth, the dashboard sends no user_id, so userId resolved to 0 and checkModerationOwnership(0, $mid) rejected every legitimate request with NOT_OWNER. Traced the origin: the legacy handler did its own checkToken() / userDatas($token), and the ADR migration in 498053179 (22 Jun) dropped that without moving the route into the auth group. It was simultaneously an IDOR for any caller that did send user_id.
  • Route moved into the auth group. The controller reads identity with $request->input(), not $request->user_id: the magic property resolves through all(), which is array_replace_recursive(input(), allFiles()) — files win — so an uploaded part named user_id could shadow the merged token value. input() never consults allFiles().
  • SubscriptionHelper::isProOrAgencySubscription() added for [1, 4, 5, 6, 8], separate from isActiveSubscription(). Sub-account included as confirmed. Known limitation now documented in the helper: code 4 is self-certifying — a sub-account whose parent org downgrades to Basic keeps subscribtion = 4 and stays eligible.
  • New PanoramaSubscriptionNotAllowedException → PANORAMA.SUBSCRIPTION_NOT_ALLOWED → 403. Ownership is checked before the plan, so a non-owner cannot use the endpoint to probe plan state.
  • No new translation key. messages.validation.subscription_not_allowed already carried the exact wording, so the exception reuses it rather than adding a panorama-specific copy to every locale. It was present in 18 of 19 locales — added the missing id translation.
  • 44 tests passing, including a new controller test proving body/query user_id and subscribtion cannot override the token, and that an uploaded part named user_id cannot shadow it. Endpoint docs and REGISTERED_APIS.md synced.

issues.display_title: Issue #1715: Return specific plan name in changeToPlan on subscription status
issues.main_description_html:
Context

FE wants the "Subscription Status" popup to name the downgrade target plan:

Your account is downgraded to {target_plan}, but you'll keep your {plan} status until your billing cycle ends

GET /v2/payment/subscription/status already returns changeToPlan, but the value is too coarse to use as {target_plan}.

Current behavior

app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Actions/GetSubStatus.php:85-86

$state['changeToPlan'] = $this->userClass
    ->checkSubType($unsubscribedData['change_to_plan'] ?? '')['type'] ?? null;

UsersClass::checkSubType() (app/Class/UsersClass.php:259-308) groups plans and drops the billing cycle:

subs code current changeToPlan
2, 7 Basic
1, 6 Pro
5, 8 Agency
0, 100 PayAsYouGo
4 SubAccount
9, 88, 99 ""

So a downgrade from Pro Yearly to Basic Yearly is reported as just "Basic".

Expected

Use UsersClass::getSubsName() (app/Class/UsersClass.php:310-343) instead — the same helper that produces subs_name in the user-detail response (app/Http/Controllers/User/Account/Action/DetailUser.php:153-154). That keeps changeToPlan in the exact format the FE already renders for the current plan.

subs code expected changeToPlan
2 Basic
7 Basic Yearly
1 Pro Monthly
6 Pro Yearly
5 Agency
8 Agency Yearly
4 Sub Account
0, 100 Pay as You Go
9, 88, 99 ""

Acceptance criteria

  • Pending downgrade Pro Yearly (6) → Basic Yearly (7) returns changeToPlan: "Basic Yearly"
  • Pending downgrade Agency (5) → Pro Monthly (1) returns changeToPlan: "Pro Monthly"
  • Format is byte-identical to subs_name from the user-detail endpoint for the same subs code
  • Unmapped codes still return "" (keep the existing ?? '' fallback at GetSubStatus.php:134)
  • No pending downgrade → changeToPlan unchanged ("")
  • Other response fields (subscription, downgrade, unsubscribed, nextPayment, isProcessed) unchanged

Out of scope (found while tracing)

BillingClass::markAsUnsubscribeV1() (app/Class/BillingClass.php:576-581) only updates next_payement_date when an unprocessed row of the same unsubscribe_type already exists — change_to_plan is left untouched. A user who downgrades twice before the cycle ends keeps the first target in the DB, so changeToPlan will be stale. Separate bug, track on its own issue.

Related

FE counterpart: GoThruMedia/gothru-dashboard#4164

Dev Note — After Implementation

Done in PR #1718.

  • Swapped checkSubType(...)['type'] for getSubsName() in GetSubStatus — one line. Changed inside the helper rather than at the call site so changeToPlan stays byte-identical to subs_name.
  • Deviation from the mapping table above: code 1 returns "Pro", not "Pro Monthly" — its monthly siblings Basic (2) and Agency (5) carry no cycle word, so only the yearly plans do. Side effect: subs_name on the user-detail endpoint changes too. Checked all 8 dashboard uses of subs_name — display-only interpolation, no string comparison, so it is a copy change.
  • Docs were wrong before this change, not just outdated: USAGE listed values the endpoint never returned ("basicy", "proy"), told integrators to validate the field against checkSubType(), and its downgrade example showed an impossible subscription: true alongside downgrade: true (the Stripe block is gated on !$state['downgrade']). The FLOWCHART sequence diagram documented a call that no longer happens. All corrected.
  • Added UserClassSubsNameTest — 14 tests, no DB needed. Pins the PHP 8 behaviour the fix rests on: '' must not loose-match code 0. On PHP 7 the same code returns "Pay as You Go" for an empty change_to_plan.
  • The out-of-scope markAsUnsubscribeV1() staleness is now user-visible: Agency → Basic Yearly then Agency → Basic Monthly kept the old target, and the previous coarse values ("Basic" either way) masked it. Worth prioritising that ticket.

issues.display_title: Issue #1717: bug(panoramas): "Not owner" error when changing Place ID (user_id 20260)
issues.main_description_html:
Report

A user cannot change a panorama's Place ID — the request fails with a "Not owner" toast.

Affected user: user_id: 20260
Tour CID: 7068319991609668221 (tour "鷲山駅")
Sequence: #3 — file 20260724-r0024611

Steps:

  1. Open 360 Image Info at /my-tours/{mid}/edit/{pid} for that panorama.
  2. Click the pencil icon on the PlaceID row (In GoThru card).
  3. Paste a new Place ID in the Set Pano PlaceID modal, click Set.
  4. Red toast: Not owner. Place ID is not changed.

The user does own this tour — it's listed under their own My Tours.

Where it comes from

POST /panoramas/change-placeid → ChangePanoPlaceIdAction throws PanoramaNotOwnerException (PANORAMA.NOT_OWNER) when ToursRepository::checkModerationOwnership($userId, $moderationId) returns false.

Hypotheses to check, in order

A. user_id never reaches the action.
The route is registered outside the auth middleware group, so the controller reads user_id from the request body. The dashboard does not send user_id in that request — only mid, pano_id, place_id. If that's the case the check runs with 0 and fails.

→ First thing to determine: does this reproduce for every user, or only some? If it fails for everyone, this is the cause and it's a full outage of the feature, not a per-user issue.

B. The moderation row is owned by a different account.
If some users succeed, compare moderation.user_id for CID 7068319991609668221 against 20260. Likely candidates: the tour belongs to a parent/agency account and 20260 is a sub-account, or the tour was transferred between accounts.

→ If this is it, the ownership check needs to accept the parent-account relationship the same way the rest of the tour endpoints do — please check how other panorama/tour actions resolve ownership for sub-accounts and stay consistent.

Done when

  • Root cause identified and stated on this issue (A, B, or something else).
  • User 20260 can change the Place ID on that panorama.
  • Users who genuinely don't own a tour still get rejected — no loosening of the ownership check beyond the legitimate account relationship.
  • Regression check: the same flow works for a plain single-account owner.

Related

  • #1716 — moving this route into the auth group is part of that task; the two overlap, coordinate so they don't conflict.
  • GoThruMedia/gothru-dashboard#4165 — frontend subscription gate for the same feature.

Summary of Changes — 2026-07-27

Root cause: hypothesis A. The route sat outside the auth group, so the controller read user_id from the body — which the dashboard never sends (SetPanoPlaceID.jsx:25-30 posts only mid, pano_id, place_id). ChangePanoPlaceIdDto cast the missing value to 0, so checkModerationOwnership(0, $mid) matched no row → Not owner. Broken for every user on that path, not just 20260; hypothesis B is not involved.

It looked user-specific because only the 360 Image Info pencil calls change-placeid. The Publish / Edit flows call set-placeid, which was already inside auth and worked.

Fixed as part of #1716:

  • b3f1a8b — route moved into the auth group; user_id and subscribtion now come from the token, a body-supplied user_id is shunted to client_user_id.
  • 96a4ee7 — identity read via $request->input() so an uploaded part named user_id cannot shadow the token value; adds ChangePanoPlaceIdControllerTest.

The ownership check itself is unchanged, so non-owners are still rejected.

Re-testing: a Pro/Agency gate now runs after ownership — a Basic-plan owner gets SUBSCRIPTION_NOT_ALLOWED (403), not Not owner. Body user_id is ignored, so reproducing a specific user needs that user's token.

issues.display_title: Issue #1678: Migrate getAIRemainingCredit to ADR pattern
issues.main_description_html:
Wrap to strict Domain-Based ADR pattern: DTO + Repository + ExceptionMapper + standard response envelope.

Endpoint: GET /tours/ai-remaining-credit
Controller: Tours\ToursController@getAIRemainingCredit
Category: B — already delegates to legacy Action class, mechanical conformance pass.

Work:

  • Create DTO
  • Create Repository
  • Create ExceptionMapper
  • Wrap response in standard envelope
  • Update route to new controller
  • Add/update tests

Dev Note — After Implementation

Done in PR #1685.

  • Extracted to GetAIRemainingCreditController + GetAIRemainingCreditAction + GetAIRemainingCreditDto; route moved, old ToursController method removed.
  • New InvalidAITypeException (TOURS.INVALID_AI_TYPE → 409), registered in ToursExceptionHttpMapper.
  • ToursRepository: added getFreeAITrial, getLatestNadirToken, getBlurTokensByUsageTypes.
  • Follow-up 82b3ba9a1: fixed wrong DB connections on the new repo methods.
  • 3 unit tests, passing. REGISTERED_APIS.md synced (API #196).
